newsitem.title: USA: More U.S. corp debt deals seen amid cheaper rates.
newsitem.headline: More U.S. corp debt deals seen amid cheaper rates.

text.p: Corporate debt offerings continue to pour in as U.S. corporations rush to finance debt amid a very attractive interest rate environment, dealers said.
"The tone in the market is extremely good and issuers are capitalizing on that," said one syndicate official. "We should see more deals pour in at these levels."
Currently, the benchmark 30-year U.S.Treasury bond is yielding 6.50 percent, its lowest level since the close of December 10, 1996.
Among the new names that have emerged is a $200 million 31-year debt offering for Columbia/HCA Healthcare via Salomon Brothers Inc, dealers said.
Unofficial price talk on the A2/A-minus rated deal is seen at 80 basis points over Treasuries, dealer said.
IMC Global Inc is another name circulating the primary arena, players said.
The firm is expected to issue $150 million in 10-year debt via lead underwriter Merrill Lynch & Co.
Goldman Sachs is expected to issue $300 million in five-year debt via the private placement market, dealers said.
Unofficial price talk on Goldman's deal is seen at 50 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.

Among upcoming global issues Argentina is expected to issue a $750 million seven-year global debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said. Unofficial price talk is the 80 basis point arena, syndicate players said.

Hutchison Whampoa Finance Ltd, a wholly-owned financing subsidiary of Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, is expected to issue a US$1.0 billion global multi-tranche debt offering, syndicate sources said on Tuesday.
The A3/A-plus rated four-part deal, which is expected to come via the 144a private placement market, is expected to include 10-year, 20-year, 30-year and 40-year maturities, sources said.
Merrill Lynch & Co and Goldman Sachs & Co are expected to jointly underwrite the multi-tranche deal, they said.
The roadshow is expected to be held this week in Hong Kong and next week in New York, syndicate players said.
CEZ Finance BV is expected to sell $200 million in 10-year notes via JP Morgan Securities Inc, dealers said.
Turning to the high-yield sector, the bulk of issuance is expected to come via the private market with close to $2.0 billion in 144a issues coming to market, players said.

Flemings Cos is expected to issue $500 million in a two-part 144a debt offering. The offering is expected to include $250 million in seven-year senior subordinated notes and $250 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes, players said.
Bear Stearns is expected to underwrite the offering.
American Communications Services is expected to set $170 milion in 10-year 144a senior notes, sources said.
Amtran Inc is expected to issue $100 million in seven-year 144a notes one day this week, players said.
Federal Data Corp is expected to sell $105 million in 11-year senior subordinated notes this week as well, dealers said.
Another $275 million in a three-part debt offering is expected to come to market from Jordan Telecommunications, sources said.
The deal is expected to include $190 million in 10-year 144a notes, $75 million (proceeds) in 10-year discount notes, and $20 million of a 12 exchange preferred issue, they said.
In addition, Metronet Communications' is also expected to sell $225 million in debt.
Also, Global Ocean Carriers is expected to sell $100 million in 10-year 144a debt, players said.
Nextel Communications is planning a $350 million sale of an exchange pik preferred 12-year issue later in the week, sources said.

Looking ahead, Raytheon Co is expected to sell $2.5 billion in a three-tranche debt offering via Morgan Stanley & Co next week. The deal is expected to include five-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities, dealers said.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
